mainTopic: Strict demand or mere suggestion (קפידא / מראה מקום); misleading a woman 'for the better' in money versus lineage; and betrothal on condition that he is a reader or a שונה.
overview: The גמרא quotes a משנה about a plain document (גט פשוט) and a folded-and-tied document (גט מקושר), and where the witnesses sign on each. רב אשי explains that the real dispute is whether a request to a scribe is a strict demand (קפידא) or only a suggestion (מראה מקום). The גמרא shows that רבי אלעזר also holds the idea of מראה מקום, from his ruling about a woman's agent who received her גט in a different place. עולא then limits רבי שמעון's view to a man who misled a woman 'for the better' in money. If he turned out to be of better lineage, everyone agrees she is not מקודשת, because she does not want 'a shoe bigger than my foot.' A ברייתא supports עולא, and רב אשי brings a proof from the משנה. מר בר רב אשי challenges that proof, and the גמרא defends it in two ways. Next comes a ברייתא about betrothing 'on condition that I am a reader,' with רבי יהודה requiring him to know the accepted translation. The amud ends with a dispute over what 'on condition that I am a שונה' means, and a challenge to רבי יוחנן's view.

steps.title: Where the witnesses sign on a plain document and on a tied document
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that on a גט פשוט the witnesses sign inside, and on a גט מקושר they sign on the back. If they sign the wrong way, both documents are invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: A plain document: its witnesses sign inside it. A tied document: its witnesses sign on its back. A plain document whose witnesses signed on its back, and a tied document whose witnesses signed inside it, are both invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה that sets the rules for where witnesses sign on two kinds of documents. It also gives the first opinion, the תנא קמא: signing the wrong way makes the document invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two types of documents, and each has its own proper place for the signatures. The תנא קמא holds that the form must match the signing: if they are mixed up, the document is פסול. The rest of the sugya will build on this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A plain, ordinary document that is not folded
A folded-and-tied document, where the witnesses sign on the back of each fold
Inside it, on the written side
On its back
Invalid

phrases.english: A plain document: its witnesses sign inside it.
phrases.notes: This is a משנה from בבא בתרא 160a. Here גט means any legal document, not only a divorce.

phrases.english: A tied document: its witnesses sign on its back.
A plain document whose witnesses signed on its back,
and a tied document whose witnesses signed inside it —
both of them are invalid.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each document type has its own proper signing place. If they are swapped, the document is invalid according to the תנא קמא.

steps.title: A tied document signed inside is still valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל holds that a גט מקושר signed inside is כשר, because it can be untied and turned into a plain document.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says: A tied document whose witnesses signed inside it is valid, because one can make it into a plain document.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the משנה disagrees about one of the two cases: the tied document that was signed inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is simple. Untie the folds, and you have a plain document with the signatures inside, which is exactly how a plain document should be signed. He does not give the reverse case the same leniency, since a plain document cannot be turned into a tied one.

keyTerms.meaning: Valid
Because one is able to make it into

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel says:
A tied document whose witnesses signed inside it is valid,
because one can make it into a plain document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא about the tied document signed inside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט מקושר signed inside is כשר, since it can be turned into a גט פשוט.

steps.title: Everything follows local custom
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that everything depends on the custom of the place (מנהג המדינה).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Everything follows the custom of the region.
steps.whatsHappening: The third opinion in the משנה says the deciding factor is what people in that place usually do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, which type of document to use depends on local custom. This sounds as if he is adding something the תנא קמא did not hold. The גמרא will question that in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The custom of the region or place
Everything

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Everything follows the custom of the region.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The type of document follows local custom.

steps.title: Does the first opinion really ignore local custom?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does the תנא קמא really reject following local custom?
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: Does the תנא קמא not accept regional custom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the way the משנה seems to read. It is setting up רב אשי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is hard to believe that any תנא would ignore local custom. If he obviously accepts it, then what is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adding? The גמרא needs to find the real point of their disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (in an earlier place)
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה
He does not hold

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
phrases.notes: This points back to the discussion of this משנה in its own place, in בבא בתרא.

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא לֵית לֵיהּ מִנְהַג הַמְּדִינָה?
phrases.english: Does the first Tanna not accept regional custom?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא לֵית לֵיהּ מִנְהַג הַמְּדִינָה
steps.kashyaTarget: The apparent position of the תנא קמא, which seems to ignore local custom.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Following local custom is so basic that no תנא would reject it. So the simple reading of the מחלוקת cannot be right.

steps.title: Where the scribe goes against local custom, everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that if the custom is one style and the scribe makes the other, all agree the document is invalid, because the person surely cared.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: In a place where they use plain documents and he made him a tied one, or in a place where they use tied documents and he made him a plain one, everyone agrees that it was certainly a strict demand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי starts to answer the question. He first defines the case where there is no dispute at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The setting is a person who asks a scribe to write a document for him. When the custom of the place is clear, the person surely expected it to be followed, so changing it is a real violation (קפידא). Both תנאים agree here, and that takes away the question's assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: In a place where the custom is
Everyone agrees
A strict demand; he insisted on it
Alternatively, or also

phrases.english: And Rav Ashi said:
In a place where they customarily use a plain document
and he made him a tied one,
phrases.notes: "He" is the scribe, writing the document for the person who asked him.

phrases.english: or else, in a place where they customarily use a tied document
and he made him a plain one —

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּוַדַּאי קְפִידָא.
phrases.english: everyone agrees that it was certainly a strict demand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): first defining where there is no dispute.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא seemed to ignore local custom.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone follows local custom. Going against a clear custom is a קפידא according to all.

steps.title: The real dispute: strict demand or just a suggestion
steps.stepSummary: The disagreement is where both styles are used and the person said 'make it plain', but the scribe made it tied. One view calls it a קפידא; the other calls it מראה מקום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they disagree is a place where both plain and tied documents are used, and he told him, 'Make me a plain one,' and he went and made him a tied one. One Sage holds it was a strict demand, and the other holds he was just showing him a convenient option.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his answer. He shows the exact case where the תנאים really argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no fixed custom, the only question is what the person's request meant. The תנא קמא says he insisted (קפידא), so the tied document is invalid. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he was only pointing out an easier option (מראה מקום), so the tied document is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Where they disagree
One Sage holds
Just showing a convenient option, not insisting on it

steps.whatToRemember: Every request must be read as one of two kinds: a strict demand (קפידא), which makes a change invalid, or a mere suggestion (מראה מקום), which allows a change.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of קפידא versus מראה מקום applies to any agent who changes from what he was told. That is why the גמרא brings it into the topic of agency here.

phrases.english: Where they disagree is

phrases.aramaic: בְּאַתְרָא דִּנְהִיגִי בֵּין בְּפָשׁוּט בֵּין בִּמְקוּשָּׁר,
phrases.english: in a place where they use both plain and tied documents,
and he told him, 'Make me a plain one,'
and he went and made him a tied one.
One Sage holds: it was a strict demand,
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא, so the document is invalid.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: מַרְאֶה מָקוֹם הוּא לוֹ.
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: he was just showing him an option.
phrases.notes: This is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A tied document is more work, so if the scribe did it anyway, no harm done.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי, בְּאַתְרָא דִּנְהִיגִי בֵּין בְּפָשׁוּט בֵּין בִּמְקוּשָּׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אשי's answer by showing where the dispute really lies.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the dispute to a case with no fixed custom.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנאים seemed to argue about whether local custom matters.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue only about how to read the person's request: קפידא or מראה מקום.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר also holds the idea of a mere suggestion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי אלעזר also holds the idea of מראה מקום. He validates a גט that the agent received in a different place than the woman named.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר also holds this, as we learned: A woman who said, 'Receive my bill of divorce for me in such-and-such a place,' and he received her bill of divorce for her in another place, it is invalid, but רבי אלעזר rules it valid. We see that he holds she was only showing him a place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds רבי אלעזר to the list of those who hold the idea of מראה מקום, and it proves this from a משנה about a woman's agent for receiving her גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman named a place, but the agent received the גט somewhere else. The תנא קמא calls it פסול, since he treats her words as a strict demand. רבי אלעזר calls it כשר, which shows he reads her words as just a suggestion, the same reasoning as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Receive my גט for me (appointing an agent to receive it)
Rules it valid
We see from here; apparently
He holds

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for the idea of מראה מקום: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the case of the documents, and רבי אלעזר in the case of the agent who receives the גט.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar also holds this, as we learned:
A woman who said to her agent:
'Receive my bill of divorce for me in such-and-such a place,'

phrases.aramaic: וְקִבֵּל לָהּ גִּיטָּהּ מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר – פָּסוּל,
phrases.english: and he received her bill of divorce for her in another place, it is invalid,
but Rabbi Elazar rules it valid.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר: מַרְאָה מָקוֹם הִיא לוֹ.
phrases.english: We see that he holds: she was only showing him a place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds a second תנא who holds the idea of מראה מקום, which was defined in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר holds a named detail is only a suggestion (מראה מקום).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in גיטין 65a: רבי אלעזר validates a גט received in a different place than the woman named.

steps.title: עולא limits the argument to money upgrades
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון is only about a money upgrade. With a lineage upgrade, all agree she is not מקודשת, because 'I don't want a shoe bigger than my foot.'
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The argument is only when he misled her into something better money-wise. But if he misled her into something better lineage-wise, everyone agrees she is not betrothed. Why? Because she says, 'I don't want a shoe that is too big for my foot.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's argument, and עולא tells us exactly where it applies and where it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון normally says that if the truth turned out better for her, she is still מקודשת. עולא says this only works for money. A husband of higher lineage is not 'better' in her eyes, since she may not want to marry so far above herself.

keyTerms.meaning: An improvement in money: the truth turned out better financially than he said
An improvement in lineage: he turned out to come from a better family than he said
Everyone agrees
Betrothed (the קידושין takes effect)
A shoe

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'better for her' is not judged only by money. A woman may truly care about not marrying far above her own standing.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
The dispute is about an improvement in money,
phrases.notes: He means the argument in the משנה between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון about misleading her 'for the better.'

phrases.english: but regarding an improvement in lineage,
everyone agrees she is not betrothed.
What is the reason?
"A shoe bigger than my foot, I do not want."
phrases.notes: A saying: she doesn't want a husband whose status is too high for her, just like a shoe that's too big.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of local custom and returns to the משנה's argument about misleading 'for the better.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument applies only to money upgrades. With a lineage upgrade, all agree she is not מקודשת, because she does not want a husband too far above her.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports עולא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says openly that רבי שמעון agrees she is not מקודשת when the upgrade was in lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way: רבי שמעון agrees that if he misled her into a better lineage, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what עולא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the word מודה, 'agrees.' That means even רבי שמעון, who usually upholds the קידושין when the truth is better, admits that a lineage upgrade is different.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא (a supporting source)
Agrees, admits
He misled her

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
Rabbi Shimon agrees
that if he misled her into a better lineage,
she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports עולא's statement with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's claim that רבי שמעון agrees about a lineage upgrade
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא) that states 'מודה רבי שמעון' about a lineage upgrade

steps.title: רב אשי tries to prove it from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the next משנה lists lineage cases (כהן, לוי, נתין, ממזר) without any argument from רבי שמעון. That suggests he agrees there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Our משנה is also precise this way. It teaches: 'On condition that I am a כהן' and he turns out to be a לוי; 'a לוי' and he is a כהן; 'a נתין' and he is a ממזר; 'a ממזר' and he is a נתין. And רבי שמעון does not argue there.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a second proof for עולא, this time from what the משנה leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some of these cases are lineage upgrades, like saying 'לוי' and turning out to be a כהן. Since the משנה records no argument from רבי שמעון there, רב אשי concludes that רבי שמעון agrees she is not מקודשת.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording of our משנה also shows this
A גבעוני, who is not allowed to marry into the regular community
A child born from a forbidden relationship, also not allowed to marry into the community
And he does not argue

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Our mishna is also precise this way.
For it teaches: "On condition that I am a kohen"
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the next משנה, on 49b.

phrases.english: and he was found to be a Levi;
"a Levi," and he was found to be a kohen;
a Nasin, and he was found to be a mamzer;
"a mamzer," and he was found to be a Nasin.
And Rabbi Shimon does not disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof for עולא, this time from the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's claim that רבי שמעון agrees about a lineage upgrade
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה lists lineage cases with no argument from רבי שמעון recorded

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי challenges the proof
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי points out that the same משנה has a money case with a daughter or maidservant, and רבי שמעון's argument is not recorded there either. So silence proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי objected: But the same משנה teaches: 'On condition that I have a grown daughter or maidservant' and he doesn't have one, or 'on condition that I don't have one' and he does. That second case is a money upgrade. Would you also say רבי שמעון doesn't argue there?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's proof by showing it leads to a result that cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having a maidservant is a money upgrade, since she will have less housework. We know רבי שמעון argues about money upgrades. So the fact that his argument is not written in that case cannot mean he agrees. The same reasoning breaks the proof from the lineage cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenged it
A grown maidservant who can help in the house

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi challenged it:
But what about what it teaches:
"On condition that I have a daughter
or a grown maidservant," and he does not have one;

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֵין לוֹ וְיֵשׁ לוֹ,
phrases.english: on condition that he does not have one, and he does have one,
which is a money upgrade,
would you also say he does not disagree?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's proof that relies on the משנה's silence.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's proof from the משנה's silence
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same silence appears in a money case where רבי שמעון surely argues, so silence cannot show that he agrees.

steps.title: Silence may prove nothing: a challenge to רב אשי's proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון's argument is stated once, in the first part of the משנה, and it applies to the later cases too. So the lineage cases may also include his argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he argues in the first part, and the same is true for the last part. Here too, he argues in the first part, and the same is true for the last part.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי finishes his challenge. The משנה states רבי שמעון's argument once and does not repeat it, so he claims רב אשי's proof from the משנה falls. The next step pushes back on this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי שמעון surely argues about the maidservant case without the משנה saying so, the lineage cases could be the same. On this view the משנה gives no proof either way, but steps 13 and 14 answer this challenge. עולא's view still stands, supported by the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה
The last part of the משנה
And the same rule applies

steps.confusionAlert: This attack targets only רב אשי's proof from the משנה, not עולא's rule, which the ברייתא in step 9 still supports. The attack itself does not hold: steps 13 and 14 answer it and bring back רב אשי's proof.
steps.whatToRemember: מר בר רב אשי's point: a משנה may state a dispute once at the start and expect it to carry over to later cases, so silence alone is weak proof. Steps 13 and 14 answer this.

phrases.english: Rather, he disagrees in the first clause
phrases.notes: The first part of the earlier משנה (48b), where רבי שמעון's argument about misleading 'for the better' is written.

phrases.english: and the same is true for the last clause.
Here too, he disagrees in the first clause
and the same is true for the last clause.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּלִיג בְּרֵישָׁא וְהוּא הַדִּין לְסֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge from step 11 and draws its result for the lineage cases.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only רב אשי's proof from the משנה. עולא's rule and the ברייתא stay in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב אשי's proof assumed the משנה would repeat רבי שמעון's argument in every case. In fact it states it once at the start, and that covers everything after.

steps.title: A money case and a lineage case are not alike
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects מר בר רב אשי's comparison. A money case can share the argument stated at the start of the משנה, but a lineage case is different and would need its own mention.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, both cases are about a money upgrade, so רבי שמעון argues in the first part and the same goes for the later part. Here it is a lineage upgrade. If he argued, the משנה should have said so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against step 12 and brings back רב אשי's proof that רבי שמעון agrees in lineage cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An argument stated once can carry over to a later case only if that case is the same kind. The daughter or maidservant case is a money case, like the first part of the משנה, so it carries over. A lineage case is a new kind of case, so if רבי שמעון disagreed there, the משנה would have had to state it.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejecting a comparison)
Both this one and that one
An upgrade in money (he turned out richer)
An upgrade in lineage (he turned out of better family)
First part / last part of a משנה

phrases.english: How can these be compared?
There, both this case and that one are a money upgrade,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the first part of the משנה and the daughter-or-maidservant case.

phrases.english: so he argues in the first part, and the same goes for the last part.
Here, it is a lineage upgrade,
so if he really argued, let the משנה teach it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מר בר רב אשי's challenge (steps 11-12) and brings back רב אשי's proof from step 10. Step 14 gives a second answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the money case and the lineage cases
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An argument carries over only to cases of the same kind. Lineage is a different kind of case from money.

steps.title: The 'grown' daughter is really a hairdresser
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the daughter or maidservant case is not about money at all. 'מגודלת' means a hairdresser who would spread gossip, which is a personal, lineage-type concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: here too it is like a lineage upgrade. Do you think 'מגודלת' means truly grown up? No, it means a hairdresser. The woman says: I don't want her taking my words and spreading them to my neighbors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to answer מר בר רב אשי. The daughter or maidservant case is itself not a money case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר בר רב אשי assumed that a grown daughter or maidservant helps around the house, which is a money benefit. The גמרא reads the word as 'hairdresser.' A woman might not want a gossiping hairdresser living with her, and that concern is closer to lineage than to money. So רבי שמעון's silence there can also show that he agrees, and רב אשי's proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say instead (a second answer)
The word in the משנה: 'grown' or 'hairdresser'
A woman who braids hair, a hairdresser
My neighbors

steps.whatToRemember: Both answers lead to the same place: רבי שמעון agrees that if the upgrade was in lineage, she is not מקודשת.

phrases.english: If you want, say:
here too it is a lineage-type upgrade,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the daughter-or-maidservant case that מר בר רב אשי brought up.

phrases.aramaic: מִי סָבְרַתְּ מַאי מְגוּדֶּלֶת – גְּדוֹלָה מַמָּשׁ?
phrases.english: do you think 'מגודלת' means actually grown up?
What does 'מגודלת' mean? A hairdresser,
because the woman says: I am not comfortable
that she will take words from me
and go spread them before my neighbors.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָכָא נָמֵי שְׁבַח יוּחֲסִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to מר בר רב אשי's challenge from step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מגודלת' means a grown helper, which is a money benefit, so רבי שמעון's silence there proves nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מגודלת' means a gossiping hairdresser, a lineage-type concern, so his silence there also shows agreement.

steps.title: Betrothal on condition that he is literate
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: if he said 'on condition that I am literate,' reading three פסוקים in shul is enough. רבי יהודה requires that he also translate.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if he said 'on condition that I am literate,' once he read three פסוקים in shul, she is מקודשת. רבי יהודה says: only once he reads and translates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It brings a ברייתא about a condition that the man can read תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא sets a low bar for being called a reader: reading three פסוקים in public. רבי יהודה adds that he must also be able to translate them. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: On condition that
Literate (someone who can read תורה at a basic level)
To translate the פסוקים into Aramaic

phrases.english: The רבנן taught:
"on condition that I am literate,"

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁקָּרָא שְׁלֹשָׁה פְּסוּקִים בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת –
phrases.english: once he has read three פסוקים in the shul,
she is betrothed.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר עַד שֶׁיִּקְרָא וִיתַרְגֵּם.
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: not until he reads and translates.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֲנִי קַרְיָינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about conditions of קידושין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading three פסוקים in shul fulfills 'I am a reader.' רבי יהודה also requires translation.

steps.title: Translating on his own is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does רבי יהודה mean the man translates on his own? Elsewhere רבי יהודה himself says a word-for-word translation is a lie, and adding to it is blasphemy.
steps.simpleTranslation: He translates on his own?! But רבי יהודה taught: whoever translates a פסוק exactly as it looks is a liar, and whoever adds to it is a blasphemer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה's words in the ברייתא using another teaching of his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'translate' meant making up his own translation, רבי יהודה would be contradicting himself. He holds that a home-made translation is either a lie or blasphemy. So that cannot be what he wants from the man.

keyTerms.meaning: On his own, from his own understanding
As it looks, word for word
A liar, someone who makes things up
Curses and blasphemes

phrases.english: He should translate on his own?!
But it was taught: רבי יהודה says:

phrases.aramaic: הַמְתַרְגֵּם פָּסוּק כְּצוּרָתוֹ – הֲרֵי זֶה בַּדַּאי.
phrases.english: One who translates a פסוק word for word is a liar.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַמּוֹסִיף עָלָיו – הֲרֵי זֶה מְחָרֵף וּמְגַדֵּף.
phrases.english: And one who adds to it is cursing and blaspheming.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's requirement in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's requirement that the man translate
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה himself forbids making up your own translation, so he cannot require it here.

steps.title: He means the accepted translation
steps.stepSummary: Answer: רבי יהודה means the man must know our accepted translation, not one he makes up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, which translation? Our translation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining which translation רבי יהודה meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man is not asked to invent a translation. He must know the standard, accepted translation. This fits רבי יהודה's other teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Our translation, the accepted one

phrases.english: Rather, which translation? Our translation.
phrases.notes: He means the standard Aramaic translation everyone used, not one a person makes up himself.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Translate' means making up his own translation.

steps.title: 'Reader' versus 'I read'
steps.stepSummary: The low bar applies only when he said 'קריינא.' If he said 'קרא אנא,' he must read all of תנ״ך with precision.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only when he told her 'קריינא.' But if he told her 'קרא אנא,' she is not betrothed until he reads תורה, נביאים and כתובים with precision.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the ברייתא. The exact words the man used change what he must be able to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קריינא' just means someone who can read a little, so three פסוקים is enough. 'קרא אנא' claims real skill as a reader. That requires reading all of תורה, נביאים and כתובים accurately.

keyTerms.meaning: And this applies only (limits a ruling)
I am a reader, claiming real expertise
With precision

steps.whatToRemember: The exact wording of a condition sets the standard. 'קריינא' means three פסוקים. 'קרא אנא' means all of תנ״ך read with precision.

phrases.english: And this applies when he said to her: "I am literate,"
but if he said to her: "I am an expert reader,"

phrases.aramaic: עַד דְּקָרֵי אוֹרָיְיתָא נְבִיאֵי וּכְתוּבֵי בְּדִיּוּקָא.
phrases.english: not until he reads תורה, נביאים and כתובים with precision.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of the ברייתא in step 15 to one specific wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'קרא אנא' requires reading all of תנ״ך with precision.

steps.title: What does 'on condition that I am a learner' mean?
steps.stepSummary: A man betroths on condition that he is a 'שונה.' חזקיה says this means he learns הלכות. רבי יוחנן says it means he learns תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'on condition that I am a learner': חזקיה says this means he knows הלכות, and רבי יוחנן says it means he knows תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new condition similar to the 'reader' case: a man claims to be a 'learner,' and two אמוראים argue about what that word means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שונה is vague, so we need to know what she was promised. חזקיה says it means oral laws (הלכות). רבי יוחנן says it means the written תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who learns or reviews; the man's claim about himself
Oral laws, like those collected in the משנה
Here, the written תורה (חומש)
On condition that

phrases.english: "On condition that I am a learner,"
Chizkiya says: it means halachos,
and Rabbi Yochanan says: it means Torah.
phrases.notes: He means the written תורה, the text itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel case to the 'reader' condition: defines another self-description used in a conditional betrothal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיה: 'שונה' means knowing הלכות. רבי יוחנן: 'שונה' means knowing the written תורה.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי יוחנן from the definition of משנה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks what 'משנה' is. רבי מאיר says הלכות and רבי יהודה says מדרש. Nobody says the written תורה, which goes against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: What counts as 'משנה'? רבי מאיר says הלכות; רבי יהודה says מדרש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's view with a ברייתא that defines 'משנה,' the word related to שונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'שונה' is the same as learning 'משנה,' the ברייתא gives only two options: הלכות or מדרש. Neither one is the plain written תורה, so רבי יוחנן's definition seems to have no support.

keyTerms.meaning: Oral learning; the noun that goes with שׁוֹנֶה
Learning laws as they are drawn from the פסוקים

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה are arguing with רבי יוחנן directly. The challenge is that their argument leaves out his option entirely.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
What is "Mishnah"?
Rabbi Meir says: halachos,
Rabbi Yehuda says: midrash!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's definition from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that 'שונה' means the written תורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא defines משנה as either הלכות or מדרש. Neither opinion includes the written תורה, so 'שונה' should not mean knowing only the written text.
